newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Rato welcomes labour reform plans.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Rato welcomes labour reform plans.

text.p: Spain's Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Tuesday he welcomed a labour reform accord that is expected to be finalised this week, and the government would work to enforce the reforms as soon as possible.
"The reforms are good news and put us among the foremost European countries in terms of social stability," Rato told journalists on the fringes of a seminar.
Unions and employers ended negotiations on Monday and are putting the final touches on an agreement.
The two sides said they were meeting their respective committees on Tuesday to discuss the draft and could announce the details of a deal on Wednesday.
The agreement must be ratified by the executive committees of each side to finalise the deal. The government will then attempt to pass the reforms through Parliament.
"The government intends to put the reforms into practice as soon as possible," Rato said.
Unions and employers reached a preliminary agreement in March that provided the foundations for a final accord, and have been putting the agreement down on paper since then.
The key feature of the accord is a permanent contract which allows for cheaper severance pay in cases of unfair dismissal -- 33 days per year worked with a maximum of 24 months.
It is hoped that this new contract will encourage employers to stop abusing temporary contracts which account for a majority of new jobs created in Spain.
Employers previously complained that Spain's high dismissal costs dissuaded them from using permanent contracts.
